cells.tense: The work sits in your hands now and reads as something whole.
cells.act: draw the shape of it without the details
cells.ask: Set the details aside for a moment and sketch only the outline of a piece you're making — a line or two, no names, no numbers. Let the shape stand without your hand on it.
cells.core:
Something you made is sitting with you now and no longer needs you standing over it. That's the odd part of this stretch: the thing reads as itself, and you can let it. If it's going well, nothing is being added — the work does the shining and you're simply at the table while it does.

The next step for you is a shape. Set the details aside for a moment so an outline can show alone, then let that outline stand without your hand on it. Some of what holds will be news, and some of the detail you've been hauling around turns out to be decoration. Either way you'll know the work better, and nothing about it has to change yet.
cells.sheetLine: You can see what you made without holding it up.
cells.place: In the clean shape of things, with the details set down

cells.tense: You'll be past the work before it has arrived.
cells.act: meet the thing before you know what it is
cells.ask: Take a piece of work you've been treating as settled, put the verdict down, and meet it with no name and no plan — just what's actually there. Stay with it a minute before you move.
cells.core:
You've been a step beyond the work, and that step is costing you the thing itself. It's shining in your hands before it's finished; you've done the finishing in your head, and the people nearby are left squinting at the light. Some of them have stopped checking what you're actually holding.

What this wants is contact, not more push. Take a piece of work you've been treating as settled and meet it as though it were new to you — no verdict, no plan, no name for it yet — and find what's actually there before you take it anywhere. You'll know it half as well as you thought, which is the useful part. What you do next comes out smaller and surer, and people can look at it again.
cells.sheetLine: You've decided how it ends before it's begun.
cells.place: In the clean shape of things, with the details set down

cells.tense: The work is done and you've kept the lamp low on it.
cells.act: choose this, not that, and mean it
cells.ask: Offer a piece of work as exactly what it is. Choose it — a sentence to a person, or a line in the work — and hold that choice after the hedge would have come.
cells.core:
Something that is finished is still being carried as unfinished — offered as a maybe, handed over with the light off it. You've been the one keeping it dim, and it's been dim long enough that the people near you read it as nothing much. What's actually there isn't being seen, because the one who could show it is holding back.

What's needed is a direction, plainly chosen. Take a piece of work you've been offering half-way, say what it is, and hold that — no softening, no listing what it isn't. A sentence to one person is enough. There's no need to praise the work; you only have to stop calling it a draft. What you name, you keep.
cells.sheetLine: You finished it. You're still presenting it as maybe.
cells.place: In the clean shape of things, with the details set down

cells.tense: Something is entering right now and it is entering through you.
cells.act: notice what is newly here, right now
cells.ask: Catch what is newly present — a shift, an idea, a small change — and take it as new, not a repeat of the last time. A line about it is enough.
cells.core:
Something is entering now, and it's entering through you, and you'd tell it as if you were only the passage it came through. The one seeing clean patterns and moving on them in the same breath is you. That part is running the show and isn't being signed, so much of what you carry is invisible from the inside — including how much of it you're steering.

What's needed is simpler than looking closely. Catch what is newly present, in your own hand or your own thought, and take it as new — not the same move in a fresh coat. A line about what's arriving is enough. Then carry on as the one it's arriving to.
cells.sheetLine: It's arriving now, through you, and you read it as the day.

attempts.check: The one claim the record does not support is any statement about what the person has actually achieved or what they have actually stopped — 'becoming what you are' is a signature, not a biography, so every cell stays at the level of what the capacity is doing in a moment, never at the level of their life story. The reader could reasonably say 'I'm not dimming anything, I just don't talk about it' — so the Too Little cell locates the dimming in what gets shown and offered, at work and among people, without naming a history or a cost. The asks survive being wrong because each is one small act of pattern-seeing or choosing that teaches something about how the person holds their own work even if the read misses; the sentence that serves me more than them is any line about 'radiance' as a quality they possess — I cut that and kept radiance as something a mechanism does.
